description: Conformance vectors for agent-request-v2, the signed agent request of OpenA2A AIM (Agent Identity Management). Each vector is one HTTP request and the answer the AIM backend's agent-request-v2 verifier gives it.

The request sends statement, the JSON payload, in the X-Agent-Request header as unpadded base64url, and each entry of signatures as one X-Agent-Request-Signature header line. A signature is an algorithm name, a colon and the unpadded base64url signature; one line may carry two signatures separated by a comma. headers are the other headers the request sends.

A signature covers the DSSE v1 pre-authentication encoding of payloadType and the statement: "DSSEv1", a space, the byte length of payloadType in ASCII decimal, a space, payloadType, a space, the byte length of the statement, a space and the statement. signedText is the bytes a vector's signatures cover, which is that encoding unless the vector's name says otherwise.

Statements are compact JSON with the members in the order method, target, audience, body_sha256, agent_id, timestamp, nonce, unless the vector's name says otherwise. body_sha256 is the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the body; nonce is unpadded base64url.

The verifier's public origin is audience and its database clock reads serverTime. The agents are registered as listed, signer names the agent whose keys made a vector's signatures, and storedNonces are the nonces already stored when the request arrives.

want is the answer: the HTTP status, the reasonCode of a refusal, and nonceStored, whether the request leaves its nonce stored. A request answered 200 reaches the route handler; a refused request does not.

Each key is derived from its label: the Ed25519 seed (RFC 8032) and the ML-DSA-65 seed (xi of FIPS 204 ML-DSA.KeyGen_internal) are the SHA-256 of the label's UTF-8 bytes. Public keys are standard base64. ML-DSA-65 signatures use the deterministic variant of FIPS 204 ML-DSA.Sign with an empty context. These keys are test values and protect nothing.
